title: File upload attack review
when: An app accepts files from users and the upload path must be reviewed for attacks: script carrying files, zip and pixel bombs, name tricks, type confusion and unsafe serving.
prompt:
Goal: Each attack class is tried against the upload feature, and every gap gets a finding and fix.
Steps:
1. Script carrying files: SVG with <script> or onload, HTML named .jpg, PDF with JavaScript; they must be refused, or served as attachment from another origin with nosniff and CSP sandbox.
2. Type confusion: magic bytes must match the declared and allowed type; names like shell.php.jpg or a.jpg%00.php change nothing.
3. Size: request cap, user quota, pixel limit before decoding (width * height under about 40 million), archive caps on entry count and unpacked size.
4. Names: stored names are generated; original names are metadata only, stripped of control characters and separators; archive entries are checked for ../.
5. Processing: conversions run in a separate process with time and memory limits on a copy; strip EXIF location from shared photos.
6. Access: download URLs check owner or share rights and are not guessable listings.
Quality bar:
- Uploaded files are never executed or included as code.
- Each attack has a sample in test/fixtures/uploads/ and an expected result.
- Findings cite file, line and fix.
Pitfalls:
- SVG uploads served inline on the main origin.
- Checking the extension only.
- Decoding huge images in the request path.
Verify:
- [ ] SVG and HTML uploads cannot run script on the app origin.
- [ ] Magic bytes are checked.
- [ ] Zip and pixel bombs hit caps.
- [ ] Downloads check access.
Output: An upload section in SECURITY-AUDIT.md and attack samples in test/fixtures/uploads/.

examples.input: testa se o upload de avatar aceita arquivo malicioso
examples.output: SVG with onload served inline found, magic byte check, pixel cap, attachment plus sandbox fix
